description:
Positron Emission Tomography has been performed for the first time in Armenia․ Instead of traveling to another country, cancer patients can now apply to the Radioisotope Production Center.

On June 10, RA Minister of Health Arsen Torosyan announced on his Facebook page that the first Positron Emission Tomography (PET/CT) was performed after 10-year wait.

"Probably from next week, all our citizens, especially those with cancer, who have been screened for PET/CT with the FDG-18 isotope, will be able to go to the Radioisotope Production Center. They will not have to look for that service elsewhere now or later.

This is a real victory for our country. I thank all those who contributed to this accessible service in Armenia, from physicists to doctors," he wrote.

It should be noted that PET/CT (Positron Emission Tomography) is a very necessary examination to monitor the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. Previously, people with cancer had to travel to Georgia, Russia, and a number of European countries for this research.
